overview: Black answers 1.c4 with a Dutch-style ...f5, intending ...Nf6, ...e6 and ...g6 or a Stonewall; White usually plays g3, Bg2, Nc3 and Nf3 and often e4 or d4. Black gets kingside space and attacking chances, but the king is weakened and the e8-h5 diagonal and e5 square need care. Play is flexible and often transposes to Dutch structures.

white_ideas.idea: Fianchetto with g3 and Bg2, pressure on e5 and the long diagonal
Take the centre with d4 or e4 and use Qb3 and the e6 weakness against ...f5

black_ideas.idea: Dutch structure with ...Nf6, ...e6, ...d5 (Stonewall) or ...d6 and ...e5 (Leningrad) for kingside play
Control e4 and play for a kingside attack with ...Ne4 and ...g5 ideas

typical_structures.structure: Dutch Stonewall or Leningrad structure with a White fianchetto

character.notes: Dutch-style play with a weakened kingside is known for imbalance and attacks for Black, riskier than most replies to 1.c4.

structure.notes: Not decided; Stonewall or Leningrad pawn structures depend on later moves.

approach.notes: Chosen by strong players in the Dutch family and regular; not a system.

level.notes: Needs understanding of Dutch pawn structures; moderate theory.

sublines_that_differ.name: 2.Nc3 Nf6 3.g3
sublines_that_differ.how: Leningrad-type with a fianchetto on both sides.

character.reason: Dutch lines tend to be unbalanced with a weakened king and mutual attacks.

structure.reason: Pawn structure is not fixed after two moves and may become Stonewall or Leningrad.

approach.reason: A recognised way to meet 1.c4 though less common.

level.reason: Plans need understanding of Dutch structures.

plans.reason: Black aims at the kingside and both sides fianchetto.
